listenings.text: Hi, I'm Lena. I have worked with design awards for ten years, and I have seen thousands of entries. People think the jury studies every project for an hour. That's not true. The first time, a jury member often looks at an entry for about one minute. So the best entries show the problem first, in one or two sentences, and then the solution. The most common mistake? I have seen it many times: entries with too much text and no clear story. My advice is simple. Imagine you are telling the story to a friend from another country. If your friend understands it, the jury will understand it too.

I've been to the ceremony in Berlin twice: the first time as a guest, and the second time as a winner. And the second time was very different. Before the show, the staff told us where to sit and what to do. When it was our turn, we waited at the side of the stage, and when they called our name, we walked up. It was only thirty seconds, but my legs were shaking. After the ceremony, there was a party, and that's when the real fun started. I have never met so many designers from so many countries in one night. My advice? Bring business cards, and talk to people. Everybody is happy, and everybody wants to talk.

paras: For more than seventy years, a design award from Germany has celebrated good design around the world. Today the iF Design Award receives more than ten thousand entries every year, from dozens of countries. Many designers call it the Oscar of design, and for a good reason: for a product team, a win is a big achievement and a strong line in any portfolio.

The process is simple to explain and hard to win. Companies and designers submit their projects in a category: product, packaging, architecture, user experience and many more. Then an international jury of design experts looks at every entry. The jury has seen thousands of projects, so a project needs to stand out quickly: a clear problem, a clear solution and a simple story. Some entries are shortlisted, and later the winners are announced.

For the winners, there is one more step: a ceremony in Berlin. Designers from all over the world go up to the stage, take photos and meet people from other companies. Many winners say the same thing: they have never felt so proud of their work, and they have never met so many interesting people in one night.
